clusters.name: Teodor's death, 1978–1979
clusters.reason: Around your grandfather Teodor's death in January 1978, within months: your grandmother Delphine stopped cooking and went to her mother's every evening; your father Duncan took night shifts and distanced from your mother; your uncle Anton began drinking at lunch with a warning at work; his wife Celeste separated from him; your mother's anxiety rose over them; and your brother Callum had ear infections through the winter. These shifts pile up close together through the spring and into 1979, each person's trouble following another's, until your grandmother took a job at the library in May and began functioning better. Every shift in these months is a reaction in the family around the loss.

clusters.name: Odette's bed rest, 1984
clusters.reason: Around your mother's bed rest in March 1984: your grandmother Hazel came every morning to keep house, then argued with your father Duncan over how she kept it; your brother Callum stammered again after a year free of it; and you could not sleep unless your father sat by the bed. Four shifts pile up in these months, each one a reaction to the change in how your mother could function, and the trouble settled by autumn when your sister was born.

clusters.name: Hazel's Parkinson's diagnosis, 1986–1996
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Hazel's diagnosis in September 1986, within the decade: your grandfather Ambrose took over her cooking and care; your father phoned his father every night for news of her; they argued over who should help their parents; your father drank most evenings; and he fought with your mother over his evenings at their house. These shifts and reactions pile up slowly over years, with no long quiet between them, each step moving your father closer to your grandmother and further from his own household, until your grandmother moved to the nursing home in June 1997 and the trouble settled.

clusters.name: Callum leaving home, 1999–2000
clusters.reason: Around your brother Callum leaving for work up north in May 1999: your father argued with him over his plans; your mother could not settle at the thought of him so far away; your father missed days at work and sat late in the garage; your sister Ines skipped school through the autumn; your mother then took Ines with her everywhere; and by August 2000 Ines was back at school full days and passed her exams. These shifts pass from one person to the next through the autumn and winter, with your mother and sister drawing closer as your father withdrew, until Ines's functioning came back in the spring.

clusters.name: Hazel's death, 2003
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Hazel's death in January 2003: you could not sleep more than a few hours a night; you stopped going in to the bookshop and were let go in May; you dreaded buses and crowded shops and went out only after dark; until you took a job at the garden centre in November and slept through the night again. Every shift in these months is yours alone, and no one else's shows then, reaching from the loss through the spring until your functioning came back in autumn.
